parameter.name: tenantPeriodDays
parameter.description: Optional preview of one tenant's own periods by table key (days, forever or inherit); needs tenantUserGroupId and covers that tenant only.

parameter.name: tables
parameter.description: One entry per table: table, property, periodDays (the instance period; blank: keep forever), status (KEEP_FOREVER, DRY_RUN), cutoff, rows, dependentRows, byTenant, byTenantPeriod {tenant: days, blank for forever} for tenants with a period of their own.

service.description: The retention periods in force: per table the instance period (days, blank = keep forever, and where it comes from: ROW, PROPERTY or DEFAULT), every tenant's own period (blank = that tenant keeps the table forever), the nightly purge days, the delete batch size, and whether the retention job is paused. A table with no period and no tenant override is kept forever.

service.description: Sets, for the instance or for one tenant, how long each table keeps its rows. periods maps a table key (AUDIT_FINDING, RUN_RESULT, AGENT_MESSAGE, AGENT_QUERY_LOG, SYNC_PULSE_SAMPLE) to a whole number of days from 1 to 3650, to forever, or (a tenant only) to inherit (drop the tenant's own period and follow the instance's). A tenant's own period, including forever, wins over the instance period for that tenant's rows only. Refused as a whole, with the reason and nothing saved: an unknown table, a value that is not one of those, inherit at instance level, an unknown tenant, forever at instance level while a JVM property pins the period, forever at instance level for a table whose period has a default (SYNC_PULSE_SAMPLE: removing the setting brings back its 30 days; a tenant's own period may still be forever). A table whose period does not change is skipped. While the retention job is running (not paused), a change that keeps rows for less time (a shorter period, or forever to days) needs previewedRows, the total dryRun#Retention showed for the same change: the preview is run again and the change is refused when today's count is more than 100 rows or 5% above it. Lengthening, and any change while the job is paused, needs no preview. Instance periods go through the settings store (one AdminAuditLog row per table, `key: old -> new (note)`); a tenant's go to its own TenantRetentionPeriod rows (one AdminAuditLog row for the call: `TABLE: before -> after`).

parameter.name: tenantUserGroupId
parameter.description: The tenant to set periods for; blank sets the instance periods.

parameter.name: periods
parameter.description: Table key to days, forever or inherit.

parameter.name: previewedRows
parameter.description: Rows the preview showed; needed to shorten a period while the retention job runs.

parameter.name: changed
parameter.description: The tables that changed: table, mode (days, forever, inherit), before, after (effective days).

parameter.name: previewNote
parameter.description: What the preview guard compared, when it ran.

return.message: Nothing to change: send periods, for example [AUDIT_FINDING: 90].
